title: DICT: No money stolen from accounts in reported government data breaches
summary: No money was stolen from accounts in connection with reported data breaches involving several government agencies, based on the information currently available to the Department of Information and…

blocks.text: No money was stolen from accounts in connection with reported data breaches involving several government agencies, based on the information currently available to the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), Secretary Robert Joseph De Claro said.

“What I know is that in terms of critical breaches, wala namang nanakaw sa mga accounts in terms of monetary. So the breaches are information that are typically already out there,” he said in an interview on the sidelines of the 2026 ROK-Philippines-ASEAN AI+ Connectivity Forum in Makati City on Thursday.
(What I know is that, in terms of critical breaches, no money was stolen from the accounts. So the breaches are information that are typically already out there.)
The DICT is continuing to examine and investigate the reported data breach at the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).

De Claro said that the DICT monitors government agencies for possible cybersecurity breaches. Once a breach is detected, the agency concerned is immediately notified and required to submit a report within two hours.

“In some cases, mas malawak yung investigation. So kaya siguro hindi pa nalalabas yung results. But I think in due time, malalabas na yung results with regards to ano ba yung data breach na nangyari,” De Claro said.

(In some cases, the investigations are more extensive, which may explain why the results have not yet been released. However, I believe the findings on what exactly happened in the data breach will be made public in due time.)
The DICT chief also acknowledged that cyber threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated, particularly with the use of artificial intelligence (AI).

In response, the DICT is working to strengthen the country's cybersecurity capabilities while pursuing broader regional cooperation with fellow ASEAN member states and countries with more advanced cybersecurity technologies.

“When you talk about cybersecurity, we really need to enhance our regional cooperation with our ASEAN brothers and also work with more advanced countries that protect and build cybersecurity solutions,” De Claro said. —VBL, GMA News
